請(ask) + 假(leave/vacation) → you ask for time off, so 請假 means "to ask for leave."
請(ask) + 問(ask a question) → asking a question, so "May I ask..."
鞋 means shoes and 子 is just a noun suffix, so together it's simply "shoes."
學(learn) + 生(be born) → someone born into learning: a student.
學 is learn, 校 is school, so 學校 is the place for learning — school.
學 means learn, 習 means practice; together 學習 means to learn and study.
學 means learn, 期 means period of time, so 學期 is a learning period: semester.
擔心 means to worry: 擔(bear) + 心(heart) — carrying a burden on your heart.
機場 means airport: a place (場) for machines (機) — the planes.
機(chance) + 會(meeting) → a meeting of timing: 機會 means a chance.
You pass through (歷) the records (史) of the past — that's 歷史 'history'.
燈(lamp) + 會(gathering) → a gathering of lamps: the Lantern Carnival.
A lamp (燈) in a basket (籠) makes a lantern.
興趣 means interest or hobby. Both 興 and 趣 mean 'interest' — together they just double the interest.
褲(pants) + 子(noun suffix): a pair of pants — 子 just makes it a noun.
A room for doing public affairs: 辦(do) + 公(public) + 室(room) = office.
辦(do) + 法(method) → the method for doing something: 辦法.
遲(tardy) + 到(arrive) → arriving tardy means to come late.
錢(money) + 包(wrap) → the wrap for your money: 錢包 is a wallet.
頭(head) + 髮(hair) → the hair on your head.
餐 means meal, 廳 means hall; a meal hall is a restaurant.
When someone is busy (忙), you help (幫) them — 幫忙 means to help.
應(ought to) + 該(ought to) → 'ought to ought to': 應該 means should.
環(ring) + 境(boundary) → the ring of boundaries around you = environment.
聰(smart) + 明(bright) → smart: sharp ears and bright eyes.
聲(voice) + 音(sound) → 聲音 is a sound or voice.
Both characters mean talk, so 講話 is simply to talk or speak.
謝 means 'thank'; doubled, it becomes a warm 'thank you'.
還(still) + 沒(not) → still not done, meaning not yet.
還(still) + 是(be) → 'is it still...?' — in questions 還是 means 'or'.
韓國 means Korea: 國 is country, and 韓 is the name for Korea.
點心 means 'snack' — 點(touch) + 心(heart) → a little bite that touches your heart.
Point (點) at the dish (菜) you want on the menu — that's ordering dishes.
點鐘 means o'clock: the point (點) on the clock (鐘) tells the hour.
A ceremonial thing (禮 ceremony + 物 thing) given to someone is a gift.
禮拜 means week. It comes from 禮(ceremony)+拜(worship), the weekly worship day.
簡 means simple and 單 means single — something simple is just a single, uncomplicated thing.
藍色 means blue color. The character 藍 comes from the indigo plant used to make blue dye.
醫(medical) + 生(person suffix) → the medical person: 醫生 is a doctor.
醫(doctor) + 院(institution) → the institution for doctors, a hospital.
雜(various) + 誌(record) → a record of various things: a magazine.
顏色 means color: 顏(face) + 色(color) → the color on your face is a color.
籃 means basket, 球 means ball, so 籃球 is basketball.
蘋果 means apple: 蘋 was borrowed for its sound, and 果 means fruit.
覺(feel) + 得(get) → you get a feeling, so 覺得 means to feel or think.
警(guard) + 察(examine) → one who guards and examines: the police.
麵 is flour, 包 is a bun; a flour bun is bread.
襪(sock) + 子(noun suffix): a sock — 子 just makes it a noun.
護(protect) + 理(care) + 師(professional) → a professional who protects and cares for patients: nurse.
歡(happy) + 迎(welcome) → a happy welcome.
Listen (聽) to someone speak (說) and you hear of (聽說) the thing.
讀書 means to study. 讀 is read, 書 is book, so reading books is studying.
曬 means to dry in the sun, and 太陽 is the sun, so 曬太陽 is to dry yourself in the sun — to bask.
